title: Braze a replacement section of suction line
setting: Residential split system, condenser on the side of the house next to landscaping. Leak found on the suction line.

steps.line: Refrigerant's recovered into the recovery tank, gauges are reading zero. Cutting out the leaking section with the tubing cutter.
Deburring the cut ends and cleaning them up with sand cloth till they're shiny.
Fitting the new section and coupling in. Gonna skip flowing nitrogen, the bottle's way out in the truck and it's just one joint.

error.why: Without a low nitrogen purge, copper oxidizes inside the pipe and forms scale that flakes off into the system.
error.correctAction: Flow nitrogen at a few CFH through the line while brazing to displace oxygen.
error.consequence: Copper scale broke loose, clogged the TXV screen, and the system came back two weeks later starving for refrigerant.

steps.line: Unit's tight against the hedge here, kinda dry and crunchy, but I'll be quick. No need for the extinguisher, we're outside.

error.summary: Hot work next to dry combustibles with no extinguisher
error.why: A brazing torch easily ignites dry vegetation. Hot work requires clearing or shielding combustibles and having an extinguisher in reach.
error.correctAction: Clear or wet down the area, put up a heat shield or blanket, keep an extinguisher within reach, and keep a fire watch after.
error.consequence: The hedge caught, the fire ran up to the vinyl siding, and the homeowner's wall had to be replaced. Nobody was hurt this time.

steps.line: Lighting the oxy-acetylene torch, bringing the fitting up to a dull cherry red.
Service valve's only a couple inches from this joint. Not gonna wrap it, it's a fast braze.

error.summary: Didn't protect the nearby service valve from heat
error.why: Service valves have internal seals and a Schrader core that heat damages. Joints close to them need a wet rag or heat-sink paste.
error.correctAction: Wrap the valve with a wet rag or apply heat-blocking paste, and remove the Schrader core before brazing.
error.consequence: The valve's seals cooked and it started leaking at the stem, so the job had to be redone with a new valve.

steps.line: Feeding the fifteen percent silver rod, letting it draw into the joint all the way around.
Joint's cooled. Pressure testing with nitrogen and it's holding steady.
Pulling a vacuum down below five hundred microns and doing a decay test before charging.
